transcript.text: If your oven won't come on at all (no lights, no display), please check that the mains power is actually reaching it by looking for any illuminated display or lights. If the display is on but it just doesn't heat, this is very often because the clock has reset after a power cut and left the oven in 'Automatic' mode, which prevents heating until you set it to 'Manual'. Could you tell me if the clock was flashing when you tried to use it, or if there is a specific manual/auto setting on your control panel?
yes the clock is flashing 0.00 and theres a little symbol too. power went off last night for an hour

That suggests the power cut reset the oven's internal clock. Most ovens default to an automatic timer mode after a blackout, which prevents heating until you manually override it. Please look for a 'Manual' or hand symbol on your dial or buttons, select that, and set the current time. Once done, try turning the oven on as normal.
no manual or hand symbol on mine. how do i set the clock? its a neff

On most Neff ovens, you can set the clock by turning the main function dial to '12:00' or a specific time setting (often marked with a clock icon), then pressing and holding the '+' or '-' buttons until the correct time appears. Once the clock is set, try turning the oven on using a standard bake function (e.g., 180°C Fan) without selecting any timer. Does it heat now? If not, please check that the cooker switch at the wall is fully on and that no fuse has blown in your consumer unit.
ok i set the time and it came on and heated. is that it?

Yes, that is it. The power cut reset the clock and left the oven in a 'safe' mode where it wouldn't heat until you set the time. This is normal behaviour for Neff ovens after a blackout. To avoid this happening again, try not to switch the cooker off at the wall unless necessary, as that will always reset the clock.
